# Home Environment Manager v0.6.0b65

## Clearer device card and optional information

- Replaces the misleading **Planning only** room badge with a localized **Room overview** when individual device controllers are shown. A room summary does not describe whether the device PID is active, paused or idle; those states are shown independently on each device.
- Groups PID calibration, measured fan-capacity setup and their Apply controls inside a **per-device collapsed Calibration section**. Opening one section is remembered during live renders. Unused measured-stage inputs are hidden while the original/uncalibrated strategy is selected.
- Shows actual native device state separately from requested controller mode, current humidity/temperature, applicable targets, PID demand, external supply state/name, available idle-cooldown information and sleep-pause status. Entity IDs and machine-readable reasons remain available in an expandable Diagnostics section rather than crowding the main card.
- Uses exact physical source IDs plus room identity to associate the right status sensor with each managed device. Duplicate/ambiguous matches are not guessed.

## Translations in all 38 supported languages

Adds localized room/device headings, calibration instructions, physical states, HVAC directions, data-source summaries such as **Selected mean**, **Idle**, measured-capacity setup messages, and Home/Away/Sleep/Comfort/Eco profiles. The card and the server-side PID friendly-name catalog now agree; untranslated English parameter prefixes no longer appear ahead of translated PID names.

Unsupported diagnostic codes are kept as technical details, not converted into apparent English prose. Sensor information is localized, and non-English scientific help includes a localized model/input caveat rather than falling through to untranslated English. Mathematical names and units such as PID, IMC, Kp/Ki/Kd, Cohen-Coon and lux remain technical identifiers.

## Illuminance (lux)

Room setup already recognized illuminance sources, but the ordinary reading pipeline did not carry their values through to the dashboard. Explicit lx/lux readings now work end-to-end, including **0 lx**, distinct source identities/friendly names, unit validation and freshness. Available selected readings feed the existing informational daylight history; missing light readings do not become zero.

Illuminance is **light information**, not an air pollutant, presence proof, solar-heat measurement, or a new permission to operate lights, HVAC or shades. An unavailable optional lux source no longer degrades otherwise valid room air-quality data. Lux alone cannot claim that air-quality evidence is complete.

## Unknown/unavailable warning entities are ignored

Missing, unknown, unavailable, null or empty optional **weather-warning sources** no longer create an outside-state blocker, fake active alert, or window-close recommendation. Ignored source IDs remain inspectable in dashboard diagnostics.

Actual active warning entities still apply. Missing actual weather measurements, adverse weather, invalid pollution units and existing physical hardware protections are unchanged. Ignoring an unavailable warning source does not assert that no real-world hazard exists.

## Validation and upgrade

Passed actual source/data tests for warning neutrality, retained active-alert handling, zero/invalid/stale lux, selected room inventory and daylight-history aggregation; locale/name checks for all 38 catalogs; and real Chromium card tests for translated statuses, collapsed calibration, expansion persistence, service routing, HTML escaping and mobile sizing. Previous Beta61-64 supply, cold-start, PID and sleep/cooldown regressions are retained. Hardware control source is unchanged by this release.

Tests use simulated Home Assistant data and are not a live appliance test.

Upgrade the existing integration through HACS to **v0.6.0b65**, restart Home Assistant, and reload the dashboard browser tab to load the new versioned card JavaScript. The single canonical domain remains `environment_manager`; no second integration or manual source-file replacement is required. The manual ZIP contains `custom_components/environment_manager/`.
